messages:
oncall-bot: Pager: high-severity - multiple inference nodes in eu-west-2 reporting NotReady and kubelet restarts. Impact: increased 5xx and failed stream starts. Please ack and triage. @eng-oncall @sre

jess: acked. seeing 4 nodes in the eu-west-2 infer pool NotReady in the last 2m. syncing logs now.

matt: I can take. starting runbook: cordon + drain problematic nodes, shift traffic to reserve pool, scale up warm spare group.

sre-lead: quick question - do we have any customers reporting errors directly? telemetry shows spike in 502s for /v1/generate in eu-west. rate about +18% RPS for that region.

jess: got dmesg tail from node infer-eu-12: "kernel: r8169 0000:03:00.0 eth0: link status changed" repeated, then "kubelet: NodeNotReady: Runtime network not ready" then kubelet restarted. also saw "nvidia: GPU reset: Xid 79" in /var/log/nvidia-installer.log.

matt: that matches `ip link` bounce != physical NIC flaps, looks like driver-level bounce. infra-bot, any recent kernel or NIC firmware deploys?

infra-bot: no scheduled kernel updates in eu-west-2 patch window. last infra change was autoscaler tuning 6h ago. No firmware rollout.

jess: on one node containerd logs show repeated: "failed to create containerd task: OCI runtime create failed: container_linux.go:xxx: failed to start container: container process is not running: . exit status 1" - suggests runtime crashed during pod start following kubelet restart.

matt: mitigation plan: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` 3) set routing policy to avoid eu-west-2 for stateful customers for 15m 4) scale up warm spares in eu-central and redirect LB 5) gather kernel + dmesg + nvml logs for postmortem.

sre-lead: do the drain now. jess, kick off customer comms draft for impacted sessions. include estimated time to restore.

jess: drafting: "We’re investigating increased errors in eu-west-2; we’ve moved traffic to other regions and are working on node stabilization. No data loss expected. Next update in 20 minutes"

matt: cordoning infer-eu-12/13/14/15 now. running `kubectl cordon infer-eu-12 && kubectl drain infer-eu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

oncall-bot: Note: 3 pods failed to schedule during drain due to nodeSelector gpu: true; they were rescheduled to warm-spare pool.

jess: scaling warm-spares: `k8s-autoscaler set-replicas infer-warm-spare-eu 6 -> 10` in progress.

matt: routing change applied: traffic-steer rule to deprioritize eu-west-2 for infer pool. CDN TTL cut to 30s for faster cutover.

eve: I’m seeing repeated Xid 79 GPU errors on infer-eu-13: stacktrace points to driver bug under link flap. will collect nvml logs and kernel modules list.

sre-lead: any sign of OOMs? we saw a burst earlier in the week cause OOM-kills, but current logs show restarts tied to NIC and GPU resets, not OOM. check /var/log/kern and kubelet events.

jess: kubelet events: "Node had condition: [DiskPressure=False, MemoryPressure=False, PIDPressure=False, Ready=False]" then "Kubelet restarted". no OOMKilled pod events.

matt: good. post-drain nodes are in maintenance mode. I'll reboot one with verbose logging and fetch full `journalctl -b -1` + `dmesg`.

infra-bot: kicked off a kernel watchdog capture job and collected `ethtool -S` on the affected NICs. preliminary shows rx_errors spike correlating with time window.

eve: attaching sample nvml excerpt (sanitized): `NVRM: GPU at 00000000:03:00:0: GPU has fallen off the bus.` repeated 4x. followed by `NVRM: GPU has been reset.`

matt: that suggests PCIe/slot or NIC driver interacting badly with GPU DMA on that kernel. I'll isolate by removing node from rotation and running extended memtest + stress on NIC driver.

sre-lead: customer impact: partial - some live streams in eu-west timed out and retried to other regions. Support ticket queue shows ~12 customer error reports. escalate to support for expedited handling.

jess: uploading incident ticket w/ severity: P2 -> summary & immediate mitigations. assigning to eng-runtime and infra for joint investigation.

deploy-bot: rolling back recent kernel debug flags on control plane was attempted earlier (no effect). no recent model-serving deploys to region.

matt: handoff: I’ll own node stabilization and logs. @eve, can you dive into NV driver trace with devtools? @jess continue comms. @sre-lead, keep monitoring traffic shift and error rates.

sre-lead: acknowledged. next update in 15. if nodes still flicker after repro, we’ll spin new host images without the suspect driver and rejoin.

oncall-bot: Ack recorded. Incident created: INC-2026-31415. Handoff: matt -> oncall (30m).

jess: update: routed 92% of regional traffic out of eu-west-2, error rate falling. collecting artifacts to attach to incident.

matt: rebooted infer-eu-13 with `reboot --reboot-command` and collected `journalctl` and `nv_peer_memory` traces. scheduling extended soak for 45m.

eve: found kernel module `r8169` unload/load cycles around time of flaps; moving to alternative driver `r8168` for test on one node now. will report.

sre-lead: good. if `r8168` stabilizes, plan: bake new AMI with r8168, drain & replace fleet, and schedule maintenance. document rollback steps.

jess: status update being posted to affected customers and support. will update incident doc with artifacts link.

matt: final for now: nodes isolated, traffic steering in place, warm spares scaled, nvml + kernel artifacts uploaded. handing to post-incident review queue once soak completes. taking ownership of remediation.

sre-lead: thanks team. stand down unless flaps return. :thumbsup:
